outcome: Child height and weight z scores
cohort: 802 mother-child pairs from the Steps to healthy development of Children (STEPS) birth cohort study in Turku, Finland
finding: In children of secretor mothers, higher HMO diversity and lacto-N-neo-tetraose (LNnT) concentration were associated with lower height and weight z scores, while higher 2'-fucosyllactose (2'FL) concentration was associated with higher height and weight z scores, suggesting a potential link between maternal HMO composition and childhood growth.
mod_finding: This study found that maternal HMO composition was associated with child height and weight z scores after adjusting for mode of delivery and other factors.
